key: Ye will not attain unto piety until ye spend of that which ye love.
s: After a ransom of gold is refused to those dying in disbelief, the surah turns to giving; al-Tabari, on 3:92, reads the piety as God’s kindness in bringing them into His Garden, reached by giving from the wealth they most wish to keep.
src: al-Tabari, Jāmiʿ al-bayān, on 3:92, the Arabic text of the Tarteel QUL library via spa5k/tafsir_api, commit 9ae590a (2026)

opened.edition: Jāmiʿ al-bayān, the Tarteel QUL text via spa5k/tafsir_api commit 9ae590a (2026), editors’ footnotes removed
opened.locator: on 3:92 (packet.js quran 7 --verse 3.92), Abu Jaʿfar’s opening gloss, before the reports that al-birr is the Garden

evidence.words: يعني بذلك جل ثناؤه: لن تدركوا، أيها المؤمنون، البرَّ = وهو"البر" من الله الذي يطلبونه منه بطاعتهم إياه وعبادتهم له ويرجونه منه، وذلك تفضّله عليهم بإدخالهم جنته، وصرف عذابه عنهم.
evidence.gloss: By it He, exalted be His praise, means: you will not attain, O believers, al-birr, which is the kindness from God that they seek from Him by their obedience and worship of Him and hope for from Him, and that is His favour to them in bringing them into His Garden and turning His punishment away from them.
